provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Counting to 100
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers from 1 to 100.
The pupils should be able to fill gaps in a number chart.

Introduction:
We have learned to count up to 50. Today we will count up to 100.
This helps us when we count naira in the market.

Content:
Counting numbers from 1 to 100.
Filling gaps in number charts.
Using number lines to count.
Counting in groups of tens.

Class activity:
Pupils will fill in missing numbers on a chart from 1 to 100.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 51 to 60.
Fill the gap: 45, ___, 47.
What number comes after 79?

Summary:
Today we learned to count up to 100 and fill gaps in number charts.

topics.title: Place value
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify tens and ones in numbers.
The pupils should be able to write the values of numbers.

Introduction:
We know numbers have different places. Like in 45, 4 is in tens place.
This helps us understand how much things cost in the market.

Content:
Tens and ones with sticks.
Place value of two-digit numbers.
Writing values of numbers.
Example: 32 means 3 tens and 2 ones.

Class activity:
Pupils use sticks to show tens and ones for numbers like 24 and 56.

Evaluation questions:
What is the value of 7 in 75?
Write 4 tens and 3 ones as a number.
How many tens are in 60?

Summary:
Today we learned about place value and how to write number values.

topics.title: Addition without carrying
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add two-digit numbers with one-digit numbers.
The pupils should be able to solve addition problems without carrying.

Introduction:
We know how to add small numbers. Today we add bigger numbers.
This helps us when we add money to buy things at the market.

Content:
Adding two-digit numbers with one-digit numbers.
Vertical addition without carrying.
Example: 24 + 5 = 29.
Checking answers by counting.

Class activity:
Pupils solve vertical sums like 32 + 6, 41 + 3 on the board.

Evaluation questions:
Solve 23 + 4.
What is 15 + 3?
Add 52 + 7.

Summary:
Today we learned to add without carrying using vertical sums.

topics.title: Addition with carrying
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add numbers with carrying.
The pupils should be able to solve vertical addition sums with carrying.

Introduction:
Sometimes when we add, the numbers are big and we need to carry.
This is like when we have too many naira notes and need to exchange.

Content:
Carrying the ten to the next column.
Vertical addition with carrying.
Example: 27 + 8 = 35.
Step by step: 7 + 8 = 15, write 5, carry 1.

Class activity:
Pupils solve vertical sums like 38 + 9, 47 + 6 on the board.

Evaluation questions:
Solve 26 + 8.
What is 45 + 7?
Add 58 + 9.

Summary:
Today we learned to add with carrying when the sum is ten or more.

topics.title: Subtraction without borrowing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to subtract ones and tens without borrowing.
The pupils should be able to solve subtraction problems without borrowing.

Introduction:
We know how to take away small numbers. Today we take away bigger numbers.
This helps us when we give change in the market.

Content:
Subtracting ones from two-digit numbers.
Subtracting tens from two-digit numbers.
Vertical subtraction without borrowing.
Example: 48-5 = 43.
Checking answers by adding.

Class activity:
Pupils solve vertical sums like 37-4, 52-3 on the board.

Evaluation questions:
Solve 56-4.
What is 73-2?
Subtract 81-5.

Summary:
Today we learned to subtract without borrowing using vertical sums.

topics.title: Subtraction with borrowing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to subtract numbers with borrowing.
The pupils should be able to solve vertical subtraction sums with borrowing.

Introduction:
Sometimes when we subtract, we need to borrow from the next column.
This is like when we need to break a big naira note to get smaller change.

Content:
Borrowing a ten from the tens column.
Vertical subtraction with borrowing.
Example: 42-8 = 34.
Step by step: 2 is small, borrow 1 ten to make 12-8 = 4.

Class activity:
Pupils solve vertical sums like 51-7, 63-9 on the board.

Evaluation questions:
Solve 54-6.
What is 72-8?
Subtract 81-7.

Summary:
Today we learned to subtract with borrowing when the top number is smaller.

topics.title: Multiplication as repeated addition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain multiplication as repeated addition.
The pupils should be able to solve 2 and 3 times tables.

Introduction:
Multiplication is like adding the same number many times.
This helps us when we have many groups of things, like in the market.

Content:
Groups and rows of objects.
Multiplication as repeated addition.
Example: 3 × 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
2 and 3 times tables with examples.

Class activity:
Pupils make groups of sticks to show 2 × 3 and 3 × 4.

Evaluation questions:
What is 2 × 5?
Show 3 × 2 as addition.
What is 3 × 4?

Summary:
Today we learned multiplication is repeated addition and practiced 2 and 3 times tables.

topics.title: Fractions: half and quarter
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify half and quarter of objects.
The pupils should be able to fold and shade to show fractions.

Introduction:
Fractions are parts of a whole. Like when we share a biscuit.
Today we learn about half and quarter.

Content:
Folding paper to show half and quarter.
Shading to show fractions.
Half means one of two equal parts.
Quarter means one of four equal parts.

Class activity:
Pupils fold paper to make halves and quarters, then shade parts.

Evaluation questions:
What fraction is shaded if half is shaded?
Show quarter of a circle.
How many quarters make a whole?

Summary:
Today we learned about half and quarter by folding and shading paper.

topics.title: Money
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add naira coins and notes.
The pupils should be able to solve shopping problems for change.

Introduction:
We use money to buy things like in the market.
Today we learn to add money and find change.

Content:
Adding naira coins and notes.
Example: ₦20 + ₦10 + ₦5 = ₦35.
Finding change after buying.
Example: If something costs ₦27 and you pay ₦50, change is ₦23.

Class activity:
Pupils solve shopping problems like buying items and finding change.

Evaluation questions:
Add ₦15 + ₦20 + ₦5.
If you buy a book for ₦38 and pay with ₦50, what is your change?
What is ₦25 + ₦15?

Summary:
Today we learned to add naira and find change when shopping.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to solve mixed problems.
The pupils should be able to answer mental maths questions quickly.

Introduction:
We have learned many things in maths this term.
Today we practice all we have learned.

Content:
Mixed problems quiz with addition, subtraction and multiplication.
Mental maths relay race.
Examples: 24 + 5, 36-8, 2 × 6.

Class activity:
Pupils participate in a mental maths relay race in teams.

Evaluation questions:
Solve 47 + 9.
What is 63-7?
What is 3 × 4?
Find the change from ₦50 if you buy something for ₦32.

Summary:
Today we revised all we learned this term with mixed problems and mental maths.
